value: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (2001). Chapter 5: Cost and Emission Reduction Analysis of PFC Emissions from Aluminum Smelters in the United States. In a larger EPA report on high-GWP gas emissions, June 2001 (the extract carries the running header "U.S. Environmental Protection Agency June 2001" and refers to an Introduction and to the CCAP programs; the parent report title and number are not printed in the 8-page extract). References within the chapter: IEA (2000) Greenhouse Gas Emissions from the Aluminium Industry, report PH3/23; The Aluminum Association (2001).

Region: United States. Locators are PRINTED page numbers of the chapter (5-1 to 5-7). Loaded: baseline PFC emission factors by cell type (converted from TCE to CO2e), and for each of the five retrofit options the break-even abatement cost per TCE at 4% and 8% discount rate, the anode-effect reduction rate (used as emissions-reduction-potential), and per-smelter capex. The same numbers are in _measures. Incremental operating cost and benefit for the major upgrades are only given as a combined range of $1-3 million/yr (Sect. 5.4) so no opex row. TRAPS: (1) Costs are US dollars with no price year; 2001 used. (2) Costs per TCE are per metric ton of CARBON equivalent (x44/12 for CO2e), not per t CO2e. (3) Capex is per smelter and the paper never gives smelter capacity, so no per-tonne capex; $8-9 million prebake and $60-65 million Soderberg are ranges for the group. (4) Exhibit 5.4 note defines PFPB (point feed prebake) but no option is costed for it. (5) The extract has mixed use of "ton" and "MT"; metric implied. (6) Net cost includes the value of added aluminium from current efficiency gains (0.4-1.0%), so the abatement cost is net of that credit.
